title: Merging two copies: union by id, newest `at` per record, `gone` against the same or older `at` only, the hybrid clock, `told` never changing
written_in: SCHEMA_V3 0 and 2.3; DECISIONS_ROUND2 D4, H1, H6, H9, L (merge q1 to q8), M3 to M5, N1, N2, O2, O3, Q5, Q7, S3, AB watch (restoring a backup with the cloud on), AD8 (the shared ui keys restored with a new at), AE1 (keyed overrides merged key by key), AE2, AE5 (restore with the D4 clock, every list, held marks, keyed overrides, a 38.31-format backup), AF3 (ui keys removed per key), AG1 (a write after a restore never ties with it; withdrawn as worded by AH4), AH1 (a device's own write uses its own clock, D8 alone questions it; an arriving copy is held only when more than a day ahead of the receiver's own now) AH5 (keyed maps found by their shape), AI1 (an arriving copy held at the receiver's own now plus 1 ms, `told` too; a device that has seen nothing holds the same way) and AI2 (entry lists found by their shape)
notes: Every amount is made up and in whole minor units (yen).
Times are hybrid clock values written as ISO with the time zone offset (section 0). They are compared as moments, never as text: 10:00+09:00 is 01:00 UTC, 02:30+01:00 is 01:30 UTC.

Question `next_at`: the `at` a device writes, the larger of now and (newest seen + 1 ms), in now's offset; a long gap since the last write is never held [AH1, which withdraws L merge q8's cap]. Question `next_at_warn`: the same, with whether D8 asks the date first (`lastDay`, the device's last open: more than one day back or more than 40 days ahead) [D8, AH1]. Question `clock_ask`: D8's question alone, `back`, `ahead` or null. A `receive` and every `sync` step of `devices` name the receiving device's own `now`: an arriving copy is held only when more than a day ahead of it [AH1, M4]. A restore's stamp is newer than everything in the device's own copy as well as `lastSeen` [D4, AH1]. A field whose value is a map whose values all carry `at` merges key by key, whatever its name [AH5]; a field whose value is an array whose items all carry `from` and `at` merges entry by entry by `from`, whatever its name, and is restored as `steps` is [AI2]. Question `came_back`: the records removed in `mine` that the merge brings back [L merge q4]. Each record may carry `by`, the device part of its last writer [L merge q1]; `steps` and `rules` entries carry their own `at` [L merge q2]; shared `ui` carries `ui.at`, one `at` per key [L merge q6]; the copy's `rev` after a merge is the larger of both plus one [L merge q3]. A `steps` or `rules` entry is removed by its own `gone` with its own `at`, and is settled like a record: newer `at`, then `gone`, then the larger `by` [M3]. Entries carry their own `by` beside their `at`, and shared `ui` keys carry theirs in `ui.by` beside `ui.at` [M5]. Question `receive`: a copy that arrives is merged in after every `at` in it more than a day ahead of the receiving device's own now is held at that now plus 1 ms (never at the newest `at` seen), `told` too, with the warning [M4, AH1, AI1]; a device that has seen nothing (no `lastSeen`) holds the same way [AI1]; the `devices` syncs do the same. Question `newer`: which of two times is later. Question `merge`: two copies merged, lists ordered by id. Questions `merge_symmetric` and `merge_same`: whether merging A with B gives the same as B with A, and whether merging a copy with itself changes nothing. Question `devices`: a short story of edits and syncs on two devices, and the record one device ends with.

A copy held on arrival is marked `held: { came, at }`: the `at` it came with and the `at` it was held at (a `ui` key's mark is in `ui.held`). A record held once keeps its held `at`: a copy whose `at` is the mark's `came` counts at the held `at`, so the fast device takes the held value when the merged copy comes back, and its copy arriving again is not held a second time [N1]. `told` is held the same way as `at` [N2]; the earliest `told` is then kept, so the first held one stays.

Ids [O2, O3]: question `id_for` builds the id of a record the app writes for a known moment (`set:<occurrence>`, `auto:<schedule>@<due>`, `pe:<the occurrence that started the period>:<place>`, `ps:<the occurrence it stands in for>` [T1]), so two devices writing the same moment make one record and the merge keeps the newest `at`; a `devices` edit may give `make` (what the record is) instead of `id`. Question `id_ok`: whether an id has the shape section 0 gives, `<device part>-<session part>-<counter>` with a 10-character session part, or is a built id.

Ids [Q5, Q7]: `id_for` also builds `rm:<place>` (the move to Waiting written when a place with money is removed), `close:<account>` (the closing's transfer or write-off; with several records `close:<account>:1`, `:2`, in order, `n` giving the number [S3]) and `skip:<occurrence>` (the skip written when a self-logged spend is removed). So the same removal, closing or skip written on two devices is one record.

cases.title: The clock is ahead of everything seen: `at` is now

cases.question: next_at
cases.title: Now equals the newest seen: one millisecond later
cases.why: max(10:00:00.000, 10:00:00.000 + 1 ms) = 10:00:00.001, so a new write is always newer than anything this device has seen.

cases.question: next_at
cases.title: A slow clock: newest seen plus one millisecond
cases.why: This device's clock says 09:05 but it has seen a record at 10:00. max(09:05, 10:00:00.001) = 10:00:00.001, so its edit still counts as newer than what it saw.

cases.question: next_at
cases.title: Two time zones: compared as moments, written in this device's offset
cases.why: now is 01:30 UTC; newest seen is 01:15 UTC, + 1 ms = 01:15:00.001 UTC. now is later, so `at` is now, written with this device's +01:00.

cases.question: newer
cases.title: The later moment can be the smaller text
cases.why: a is 01:00 UTC, b is 01:30 UTC, so b is newer, although as text "...T02:30" sorts before "...T10:00". Comparing `at` as text would let the wrong copy win.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: Union by id: a record on each device, both kept
cases.why: Different ids, so both are in the union [D4]. Nothing is dropped.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: The same record edited on both: the newer `at` wins
cases.why: 10:05 is newer than 10:00, so the copy with 1,500 wins [D4].

cases.question: merge
cases.title: The winner's fields, the oldest `told`
cases.why: theirs wins on `at` (10:05), so a is 1,500. `told` is never taken from the winner: the oldest seen for the id is kept, 12:00 not 12:30 [H1, 2.3].

cases.question: merge
cases.title: An Undo newer than the other copy wins
cases.why: The removed copy's `at` (21 Nov 10:05) is newer than the other's (20 Nov 12:00): gone wins, with its goneBy.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: `gone` wins a tie on `at`
cases.why: Both `at` are 21 Nov 10:00:00.000. H6: a copy with `gone` wins against one whose `at` is the same or older, so the removed copy wins before any device tie-break.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: A Redo (newer, not gone) wins over the Undo it reverses
cases.why: The Redo cleared gone and goneBy and moved `at` to 10:01, newer than the Undo's 10:00. `gone` wins only against the same or older `at`, so the Redo wins [H6].

cases.question: merge
cases.title: Removed on one device, edited later on the other that never saw it: the edit wins
cases.why: H6: the removed copy (10:00) is older than the edit (10:05), so `gone` does not win and the edited record comes back with 1,350. L merge q4 confirms it: an edit newer than a removal brings the record back, and the next check-in shows "came back" (mg-30).

cases.question: merge
cases.title: A removed record on one device only is kept, still removed
cases.why: Nothing is deleted (section 0): a removed record stays in the union with its `gone`, so a third copy that still has it alive cannot bring it back unless that copy is newer.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: The same amount typed on two devices: the merge keeps both
cases.why: Two ids, so both stay. The merge never removes either; the possible double is offered to the person (matching double-01) [H9, 2.3].

cases.question: merge
cases.title: A schedule changed on both devices: the steps merge by `from`, neither step is lost
cases.why: Entries inside `steps` carry their own `at` and merge by `from` [L merge q2]. The 1 Nov step is the same on both; the 1 Dec step (typed on this device at 10:00) and the 1 Apr step (typed on the other at 10:05) are each on one side only, so both are kept, in date order. The rest of the record comes from the newer copy (10:05). Before L the whole newer record won and the December step was lost.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: A single record (`home`): the newer `at` wins
cases.why: Single records carry `at` (section 0) and merge the same way: 10:05 is newer, so minBank is null (no minimum).

cases.question: merge
cases.title: A field this page does not know stays on the winning copy
cases.why: theirs wins on `at`; unknown fields are kept (section 0), so `colour` from a newer page survives the merge.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: Lists inside the plan merge by id too
cases.why: `plan.budgets` entries are list records with id, told and at (section 0), so they are a union by id like events.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: Two time zones: the later moment wins, not the larger text
cases.why: mine is 01:00 UTC, theirs 01:30 UTC (the laptop is in Europe). theirs is newer and wins with 1,250 (mg-05).

cases.question: merge_symmetric
cases.title: Merging A into B gives the same as B into A
cases.why: Every rule above picks a winner from the two copies alone (newer `at`, then `gone` on a tie, oldest `told`), never from which side is "mine". So both devices end with the same copy: e1 removed, e2 at 950, e3 kept.

cases.question: merge_same
cases.title: Merging a copy with itself changes nothing
cases.why: Each record meets an identical copy of itself; any rule keeps it as it is. A merge sent again after a cloud conflict (2.3) therefore cannot change anything twice.

cases.question: merge_symmetric
cases.title: Same `at`, both alive, different amounts: both devices still agree
cases.why: "The device part breaking ties" (section 0) means the tie is decided by something both devices see the same way, so both end with the same record. Which one wins is in mg-26 (the larger `by`) [L merge q1]; this case only checks that they agree.

cases.question: devices
cases.title: A phone whose clock is a day fast is not held; the other device's later edit still wins, 1 ms after what it has seen (AH1)
cases.why: A's clock says 24 Nov 10:00 while B's says 23 Nov 10:04. A's own write uses its own clock [AH1]: 1,500 at 24 Nov 10:00. When A's copy reaches B, B's own now is 23 Nov 10:04, so a day ahead is 24 Nov 10:04; 24 Nov 10:00 is not more than that, so nothing is held [AH1, M4] and B has now seen 24 Nov 10:00. B edits at 10:05 by its clock: the later of 23 Nov 10:05 and 24 Nov 10:00:00.001 is 24 Nov 10:00:00.001 [D4], so 1,800 wins on both devices with that `at` (A, at its own 24 Nov 10:10, holds nothing: 10:00:00.001 is behind it). `told` never moved [H1]. Before AH1 A's own write was held at 23 Nov 09:00:00.001 [L merge q8, withdrawn].

cases.question: devices
cases.title: A phone less than a day fast wins against an edit made without seeing it (AH1: only more than a day ahead of the receiver is held)
cases.why: A writes 1,500 at 24 Nov 10:00 by its own clock [AH1]. B, not having seen it, writes 1,800 at 23 Nov 10:05. B's copy reaches A (A's now 24 Nov 10:10): 23 Nov 10:05 is older, A keeps 1,500. A's copy reaches B (B's now 23 Nov 10:10, so a day ahead is 24 Nov 10:10): 24 Nov 10:00 is not more than a day ahead, so it is not held [AH1, M4] and, being newer, 1,500 wins on B too. A clock up to a day fast can win this way; a wrong clock more than a day ahead of the receiver is held. Before AH1 A's own write was held at 23 Nov 09:00:00.001 and 1,800 won [L merge q8, withdrawn].

cases.question: devices
cases.title: A record made on one device and edited on the other keeps its first `told`
cases.why: The record is made on A at 12:00, so `told` is 12:00. B's edit at 18:00 moves `at` to 18:00 and changes the amount, but never `told` (section 0, H1). So a check made at 15:00 that day still holds this spend, wherever it was edited.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: The same `at` on both, both alive: the larger `by` wins
cases.why: Both copies have `at` 21 Nov 10:00:00.000 and neither is removed. Each record carries `by`, the device part of its last writer; on an equal `at` the larger `by` wins [L merge q1]: bbbbbb is larger than aaaaaa, so 1,200 wins on both devices.

cases.question: devices
cases.title: An edit writes the device part of its writer in `by`
cases.why: The record was made on A (its id starts aaaaaa) and last written on B at 18:00, so `by` is bbbbbb, the device part of its last writer [L merge q1]. The id still names the maker; `told` stays at 12:00 (H1).

cases.question: merge
cases.title: The same step edited on both devices: the newer entry wins
cases.why: Both copies hold a step from 1 Dec. Steps merge by `from`, each by its own `at` [L merge q2]: 10:00 is newer than 09:30, so the 260,000 step wins.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: The copy's `rev` after a merge is the larger of both plus one
cases.why: The copy's `rev` is the larger of both plus one [L merge q3, q5]: 9 + 1 = 10. e1 is the same on both, so its `at` does not move: a record's `at` moves only when it changes [L merge q3].

cases.question: came_back
cases.title: An edit newer than a removal brings the record back, and the check-in can say so
cases.why: e1 was removed here at 10:00 and edited on the other device at 10:05: the newer edit brings it back, so the next check-in shows "came back" for e1 [L merge q4]. e2's copy on the other device (09:00) is older than the removal, so e2 stays removed.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: Shared `ui` keys merge one by one, by `ui.at`
cases.why: Shared `ui` keys carry their `at` in `ui.at` [L merge q6]. main: 10:05 (theirs) is newer than 10:00, so free. sb: 10:10 (mine) is newer than 10:00, so 1. win is only on theirs, so 3. Each key keeps the `at` it won with.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: A copy from an older page with no `told`: the one there is kept
cases.why: mine wins on `at` (10:05) but has no `told`. The earlier `told` is kept, and the only one there is theirs, 20 Nov 12:00 [L merge q7, H1].

cases.question: next_at
cases.title: A device used again two days after its last write writes its own now (AH1)
cases.why: The newest `at` this device has seen is Mon 23 Nov 10:00, its own last write; it is used again on Wed 25 Nov 10:00, 48 hours later. A long gap is normal and never held [AH1]: `at` is the later of now (25 Nov 10:00) and the newest seen plus 1 ms (23 Nov 10:00:00.001), so 25 Nov 10:00. Before AH1 this case said the clock was "held at 23 Nov 10:00:00.001" [L merge q8, withdrawn], and every later write stayed stuck there (confirm_review_4 item 1).

cases.question: next_at_warn
cases.title: Two days away: no warning; only D8 questions a device's own clock (AH1)
cases.why: As mg-33: `at` is now, 25 Nov 10:00. A gap since the last write is never a reason to warn [AH1]; the device's own clock is questioned only by D8 (a date that jumps back more than a day, or more than 40 days ahead of its last open), and no last open day is given here, so nothing is asked.

cases.question: next_at_warn
cases.title: Exactly one day ahead is not more than a day: `at` is now, no warning
cases.why: now is 24 hours after the newest seen: a day ahead, not more, so `at` is now and nothing is held [L merge q8].

cases.question: merge
cases.title: A step removed on one device stays removed, even when the other device edited the schedule later
cases.why: The record: 10:30 (theirs, the new name) is newer than 10:20, so the name is theirs. The steps merge by `from`, each by its own `at` [L merge q2]. The 1 Jan step was removed here by its own `gone` at 10:20 [M3]; theirs is the step as it was at 10:10, older, so the removal wins and stays in the list as a removed entry. The union cannot bring it back, and the next merge finds the same `gone`.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: A step removed and edited at the same `at`: the removal wins, as on a record
cases.why: An entry is removed by its own `gone` with its own `at` [M3], so it is settled the way a record is: the newer `at`, then on the same `at` the copy with `gone` [H6], then the larger `by` [M5]. Both steps have `at` 10:20, so the removed one wins although bbbbbb is the larger `by`. The record itself ties on `at` too and neither is removed, so the larger `by`, bbbbbb, gives its fields [L merge q1].

cases.question: receive
cases.title: A copy that arrives more than a day ahead of what this device has seen is held
cases.why: This device's own now is 23 Nov 09:30, so a day ahead is 24 Nov 09:30 [AH1]. e1's 25 Nov 10:00 is more than a day ahead, so it is held at that now plus 1 ms, 23 Nov 09:30:00.001 [AI1], marked with the `at` it came with and the held one, and the warning is shown [M4, N1]. e2's 23 Nov 20:00 is less than a day ahead and is kept. Then the merge: held e1 (09:30:00.001) is newer than mine (08:00), so 1,500 wins; `by` stays cccccc, its last writer. Before AI1 it was held at the newest `at` seen (23 Nov 09:00) plus 1 ms, 09:00:00.001, with the same result here.

cases.question: devices
cases.title: A new phone two days fast: its edit is held when it reaches the other device, and a later edit there wins
cases.why: A is new and has no `at` of its own seen, so its own write is not held: 25 Nov 10:00 [AH1]. A's copy reaches B at B's own now, 23 Nov 10:00: a day ahead is 24 Nov 10:00, and 25 Nov 10:00 is more than that [AH1], so the record is held at that now plus 1 ms, 23 Nov 10:00:00.001 [AI1], and marked `held: { came: 25 Nov 10:00, at: 23 Nov 10:00:00.001 }` [M4, N1]. B's edit at 23 Nov 10:05 is later than anything B has seen, so it is written at 10:05 by bbbbbb and wins: 1,800; the edit keeps the mark (mg-42 shows why). Before M4, B took in 25 Nov 10:00 as seen and its edit was pushed to 25 Nov 10:00:00.001. Before AI1 the held value was B's newest seen plus 1 ms, 23 Nov 09:00:00.001.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: Two steps with the same `from` and the same `at`: the larger `by` wins
cases.why: Each entry carries its own `by` beside its `at` [M5]. Both 1 Dec steps have `at` 10:00 and neither is removed, so the larger `by` wins: bbbbbb, 255,000, on both devices. Before M5 the larger sorted text won, which was 260,000.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: Two `ui` keys with the same `at`: the larger `by` in `ui.by` wins
cases.why: A shared `ui` key carries its `by` beside its `at`: `ui.by` beside `ui.at` [M5, L merge q6]. main has the same `at`, 10:00, on both, so the larger `by` wins: bbbbbb, trip. Before M5 the larger value as text won, which was waiting.

cases.question: devices
cases.title: A record held once keeps its held `at`: the fast copy that arrives again does not beat the later edit
cases.why: A writes 1,500 at 25 Nov 10:00 (its own write is never held [AH1]). A's copy reaches B at B's own now, 23 Nov 10:00: a day ahead is 24 Nov 10:00, so the record is held at that now plus 1 ms, 23 Nov 10:00:00.001 [AI1], and keeps the mark `held: { came: 25 Nov 10:00, at: 23 Nov 10:00:00.001 }` [M4, N1]. B writes 1,800 at 10:05, later than 10:00:00.001, so it wins; an edit keeps the mark (unknown fields are kept, section 0). A's copy arrives again at B's now 10:10, still 25 Nov 10:00, more than a day ahead: before N1 it was held again, at 10:10:00.001, and beat B's edit (1,500 on both). Now its `at` is the one B already held, so it takes the held 10:00:00.001 [N1]: older than 10:05, and 1,800 stays.

cases.question: devices
cases.title: The fast device takes the held value when the merged copy comes back, so the later edit wins there too
cases.why: As mg-42 up to B's edit: B holds 1,800 at 23 Nov 10:05 with the mark `held: { came: 25 Nov 10:00, at: 23 Nov 10:00:00.001 }` (B's now when the copy came, plus 1 ms [AI1]). B's copy reaches A. A's own copy is 1,500 at 25 Nov 10:00, which is the `came` of the mark, so A takes the held value, 10:00:00.001 [N1]. B's 10:05 is newer, so A shows 1,800 by bbbbbb, the same as B. Before N1 A's 25 Nov 10:00 was newer than 10:05: A kept 1,500 and B's edit was lost.

cases.question: devices
cases.title: With no edit in between, the fast device ends with the held `at` too
cases.why: A's copy reaches B at B's own now, 23 Nov 10:00: a day ahead is 24 Nov 10:00 and 25 Nov 10:00 is more than that [AH1], so B holds it at that now plus 1 ms, 23 Nov 10:00:00.001, and marks it [AI1, M4, N1]. When B's copy comes back, A's own `at`, 25 Nov 10:00, is the mark's `came`, so A takes the held value: 1,500 at 23 Nov 10:00:00.001, still by cccccc, its writer [N1]. Both devices now hold the same `at`, so any later edit on B (10:05, say) is newer on both.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: Merging the fast copy with the held one: the mark decides, in either order
cases.why: Mine is the fast device's 1,500 at 25 Nov 10:00. Theirs is B's 1,800 at 23 Nov 10:05, carrying `held: { came: 25 Nov 10:00, at: 23 Nov 09:00:00.001 }`. Mine's `at` is the `came`, so it counts as 09:00:00.001 [N1]; 10:05 is newer, so theirs wins whole, mark and all. `told` is 20 Nov 12:00 on both. Before N1 the newest `at` was 25 Nov 10:00 and 1,500 won.

cases.question: receive
cases.title: A `steps` entry held once keeps its held `at` when the same fast copy arrives again
cases.why: This device held the fast copy's 25 Nov 10:00 once, at 23 Nov 09:00:00.001, on the record and on its 1 Jan step, and then edited both at 10:05 (the marks stay). The same fast copy arrives again. Its `at` on the record and on the step is the `came` of the marks, so each takes its held 09:00:00.001 [N1, M5], not 10:10:00.001 (this device's now plus 1 ms [AI1]). 10:05 is newer on both: the name and 275,000 stay. Nothing new was held, so no warning: the warning was shown when it was first held. [AH1] A copy is held only when it is more than a day ahead of this device's own now, 23 Nov 10:10.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: A shared `ui` key held once keeps its held `at`, with its mark in `ui.held`
cases.why: A `ui` key carries its `at` in `ui.at` and its `by` in `ui.by` [L merge q6, M5], so its mark is in `ui.held` beside them. Theirs is the fast device's 25 Nov 10:00, the `came` of mine's mark, so it counts as 23 Nov 09:00:00.001 [N1]. Mine's 10:05 is newer: trip stays. Before N1 25 Nov 10:00 was newer and waiting won.

cases.question: receive
cases.title: A record made on a fast device: its `told` is held the same way as its `at`
cases.why: e3 was made on a device two days fast, so its `told` and `at` are both 25 Nov 10:00 (H1: `told` is set when the record is made). This device's own now is 23 Nov 09:30, a day ahead is 24 Nov 09:30 [AH1], so both are held at that now plus 1 ms, 23 Nov 09:30:00.001 [AI1, M4, N2], and the warning is shown. Before N2 `told` stayed 25 Nov 10:00, so e3 came after every check on 23 Nov whatever its real order. The `at` keeps its mark [N1].

cases.question: devices
cases.title: The held `told` is kept when the fast copy arrives again and when it goes back
cases.why: A makes e2 at 25 Nov 10:00: `told` and `at` both 25 Nov 10:00. A's copy reaches B at B's own now, 23 Nov 10:00: a day ahead is 24 Nov 10:00 [AH1], so both are held at that now plus 1 ms, 23 Nov 10:00:00.001 [AI1, M4, N2]. B edits at 10:05: `at` moves, `told` never does [H1]. A's copy arrives again at B's now 10:10: its `at` is the mark's `came`, so 10:00:00.001 [N1]; its `told`, 25 Nov 10:00, is still more than a day ahead, so it is held at 10:10:00.001, and the earliest `told` is kept: 10:00:00.001 [H1, L merge q7]. Back on A, its own `told` 25 Nov 10:00 against 10:00:00.001: the earliest, 10:00:00.001, so the record keeps its first held `told` on both. B's 10:05 edit (900) wins on A as in mg-43.

cases.question: id_for
cases.title: A settlement the check-in writes is named by its occurrence
cases.why: Ticking Pay at the check-in settles pay@2026-12-25, so the event it writes is `set:pay@2026-12-25` on every device [O2].

cases.question: id_for
cases.title: A spend that logs itself is named by its schedule and date
cases.why: The gym fee's own spend for its 1 Feb occurrence is `auto:gym@2027-02-01`, whichever device writes it [O2]. The date is the occurrence's due date before any move, as in every occurrence name [H2].

cases.question: id_for
cases.title: A period-end answer is named by the pay that started the period and its place
cases.why: The answer for what was left in Free to spend in the period begun by pay@2026-11-25 (it ended Thu 24 Dec) is `pe:pay@2026-11-25:free` [O2, T1]: a period is named by the occurrence of its pay, never by a day that can move.

cases.question: id_for
cases.title: A period started without the pay is named by the pay it stands in for
cases.why: A period start the person chose for Sun 20 Dec, standing in for the pay due Fri 25 Dec, is `ps:pay@2026-12-25`; the day they chose is its `date` [O2, N5, T1].

cases.question: devices
cases.title: Jun and Tess each tick Pay on their own phone: one record, the newest `at`
cases.why: Both ticks settle pay@2026-12-25, so both phones write `set:pay@2026-12-25` [O2]. The merge joins them as one record: Tess's 248,000 at 08:02 is newer than Jun's 250,000 at 08:01, so it wins; `told` keeps the earliest, 08:01 [L merge q7]. Bank: 50,000 + 248,000 = 298,000, never 548,000.

cases.question: restore
cases.title: AB watch: restoring an older backup with the cloud on writes `gone` with a new `at` for what is newer and gives the backup's records a new `at`
cases.why: A backup saved Tue 10 Nov holds a spend of 1,000, a spend of 3,000 and the pay schedule (250,000 from 1 Nov). After it, with the cloud copy on, the desktop changed the 1,000 to 1,500 (15 Nov), added a spend of 2,000 (16 Nov), removed the 3,000 (17 Nov) and added a pay step of 260,000 from 1 Dec (18 Nov). On Sat 21 Nov at 09:00 the phone restores the backup. The restore [AB watch]: the 2,000 spend is not in the backup, so it is written `gone` (the restore's day, 21 Nov) with `at` 21 Nov 09:00 and `by` phn001; the 1,000 spend and the 3,000 spend are the backup's, so they come back as the backup holds them (1,000, and the 3,000 with no `gone`), each with `at` 21 Nov 09:00. The pay schedule is the backup's with a new `at`; its 1 Nov step is the backup's with a new `at`, and the 1 Dec step, newer than the backup, is removed by its own `gone` with its own new `at` [M3]. `told` stays the first one each record had [H1]. [AH1] The phone has seen the cloud copy up to 18 Nov 10:00 (`lastSeen`). That gap is never held: the restore stamps the later of now (21 Nov 09:00) and 18 Nov 10:00:00.001, so 21 Nov 09:00. Before AH1 this input left `lastSeen` out, because with it the restore was held at 18 Nov 10:00:00.001 (confirm_review_4).

cases.question: restore_merge
cases.title: AB watch: the merge with the cloud copy keeps the restore, on either side
cases.why: A backup saved Tue 10 Nov holds a spend of 1,000, a spend of 3,000 and the pay schedule (250,000 from 1 Nov). After it, with the cloud copy on, the desktop changed the 1,000 to 1,500 (15 Nov), added a spend of 2,000 (16 Nov), removed the 3,000 (17 Nov) and added a pay step of 260,000 from 1 Dec (18 Nov). On Sat 21 Nov at 09:00 the phone restores the backup. Each restored record and step has `at` 21 Nov 09:00, newer than every `at` in the cloud copy (the newest is 18 Nov 10:00), so per record and per step the restore wins [D4, M3]: the 1,000 spend at 1,000, the 3,000 spend back, the 2,000 spend and the 1 Dec step gone. `told` is the earliest seen, the same on both sides. Merged either way round it is the restored copy. Before this rule the union merge brought every newer record back at the next sync, so a restore rolled nothing back. [AH1] The phone has seen the cloud copy up to 18 Nov 10:00 (`lastSeen`). That gap is never held: the restore stamps the later of now (21 Nov 09:00) and 18 Nov 10:00:00.001, so 21 Nov 09:00. Before AH1 this input left `lastSeen` out, because with it the restore was held at 18 Nov 10:00:00.001 (confirm_review_4).

Per key [AE1]: December goes to the newer key, the desktop's 60,000 (10:05 after 10:00); January's removal (10:10) is newer than the desktop's 1 Nov key, so it stays removed [M3]. cases.question: merge
cases.title: AE1, AE2: the pay day answered on the phone writes January's waiting 0; a rename on the desktop before the sync keeps it
cases.why: Both devices moved the same 38.31 copy (last saved Mon 23 Nov 20:00), which holds January 2027 pay of 0 waiting for the pay day. On Sat 28 Nov 08:00 the phone answers: the 25th. That adds a `rules` entry (the answer's `at`) and writes January's 0 on the 25 Jan pay, the key carrying the entry's `at`, 23 Nov 20:00 [AE2]; the entry is kept `gone` with the answer's `at`. On Sun 29 Nov the desktop, not yet synced, renames the pay. At the merge the record goes to the desktop (29 Nov): "Salary (Acme)". The `rules` entry and the `amounts` key are only on the phone and merge by entry and by key [L merge q2, AE1], so both stay: January counts 0, not 250,000. The waiting entry: the phone's `gone` (28 Nov 08:00) is newer than the desktop's live copy (23 Nov 20:00), so it is not applied again (confirm_review_3 item 1, the worst chain).

cases.question: receive
cases.title: AE1, M4, N1: a key that arrives more than a day ahead is held, with its own mark
cases.why: This device's own now is 24 Nov 10:05, so a day ahead is 25 Nov 10:05 [AH1]. A device with its clock three days fast sends the pay with December's 0 written at 27 Nov 10:00. The record and the key are each held at that now plus 1 ms, 24 Nov 10:05:00.001 [AI1], each marked with the `at` it came with and the held one [M4, N1, AE1], and the warning is shown. Then the merge: the held record (10:05:00.001) is newer than mine (1 Nov), and the key is only in the arriving copy, so December's 0 is kept with its mark.

cases.question: restore_merge
cases.title: AE5: a restore on a device whose clock is behind stamps with the D4 clock, from the newest `at` in its own copy, so the merge still keeps it
cases.why: The backup (Tue 10 Nov) holds a spend of 1,000. Since then the desktop changed it to 1,500 (Wed 18 Nov 10:00) and added a spend of 2,000; the phone has seen both: they are in its own copy (no separate `lastSeen` needed). The phone's clock is behind: it reads Tue 17 Nov 09:00 when the backup is restored. The restore stamps with the D4 clock [AE5]: the larger of now and the newest `at` seen plus 1 ms, 18 Nov 10:00:00.001. So the 1,000 comes back and the 2,000 is `gone` (the restore's day, 17 Nov), each with that `at`, newer than every `at` in the cloud copy, and the merge keeps the restore either way round. With the raw time (17 Nov 09:00) the desktop's 1,500 (18 Nov) would come back: only part of the restore would hold (confirm_review_3, restore column). [AH1] What the device has seen includes its own copy, so the newest seen is 18 Nov 10:00 without a `lastSeen` in the input. Before AH1 the input named `lastSeen` (COVERAGE, AE and AF table) and the restore ignored the copy.

cases.question: restore
cases.title: AE5: a restore covers records with built ids (`set:`, `pe:`, `mv:draw:`) like any other
cases.why: The backup (Thu 26 Nov 07:00) holds the moved Emergency fund draw `mv:draw:once.2027-01` (20,000) and October's period-end answer `pe:pay@2026-10-25:free` (1,500 to Waiting). After it the desktop changed the draw to 15,000 (12:00), ticked the 25 Nov pay, writing `set:pay@2026-11-25` (12:30), and changed the answer to 2,000 (13:00). On Fri 27 Nov 09:00 the phone restores the backup [AE5]. Built ids are records like any other: the draw comes back at 20,000 and the answer at 1,500, each with the restore's `at` and `by`; the settle is not in the backup, so it is `gone` (27 Nov) with the restore's `at`, and the 25 Nov pay is expected again. `told` stays each record's first [H1].

cases.question: restore
cases.title: AE5: a restore covers `pendingMove`, the frozen texts and keyed overrides: what waited at the backup waits again
cases.why: The phone moved its 38.31 copy (last saved Mon 23 Nov 20:00) and made a backup before answering anything: January's pay of 0 waits in `pendingMove`. Later the desktop moved too (its frozen text `mv:frozen:dsk001`), and on Sat 28 Nov the phone answered the pay day, the 25th: a `rules` entry, January's 0 as `amounts` on 25 Jan, the entry `gone`. On Sun 29 Nov 09:00 the phone restores the backup [AE5]: the schedule, its step, the waiting entry and the phone's frozen text come back as the backup holds them, each with the restore's `at`. What is newer than the backup is removed by its own `gone` (29 Nov) with that `at`: the `rules` entry [M3], the `amounts` key [AE1] and the desktop's frozen text. So the pay day is asked again and January's 0 waits for it again.

cases.question: restore_merge
cases.title: AE5, N1: a restore keeps the held marks the device knows, so the fast device's copy cannot beat the restore
cases.why: A device with its clock two days fast changed a spend to 5,000, written at Thu 26 Nov 10:00. The phone, which had seen up to Tue 24 Nov 10:00, held it at 24 Nov 10:00:00.001 with the mark { came 26 Nov 10:00, at 24 Nov 10:00:00.001 } [M4, N1]. The backup (Mon 23 Nov) holds 4,000. On 24 Nov 12:00 the phone restores it [AE5]: 4,000 with the restore's `at` (12:00), and the record keeps the held mark the phone knows, as an edit keeps it [N1]. The fast device's own copy in the cloud still says 26 Nov 10:00: that is the mark's `came`, so it counts at the held 24 Nov 10:00:00.001 and the restore (12:00) wins, either way round. Without the mark the 26 Nov copy would win and the restore would not hold.

cases.question: restore_merge
cases.title: AE5, AE1: a restore covers keyed overrides key by key; the merge with the cloud copy keeps it
cases.why: The backup (Tue 24 Nov 09:00) holds December pay of 50,000 (`amounts` key 2026-12-25), the car loan with no extra and Food with no `once`. After it: December pay changed to 0 (10:00), January pay set to 100,000, 30,000 extra planned on the loan from January, and Food 70,000 for the December period (all 25 Nov). On Thu 26 Nov 09:00 the phone restores the backup [AE5]. Key by key [AE1]: December pay back to 50,000 with the restore's `at`; January's key, the January extra and Food's December key are not in the backup, so each is removed by its own `gone` (26 Nov) with the restore's `at`; the steps and the loan's first extra entry get the new `at` [M3]. Every stamp is 26 Nov 09:00, newer than the cloud copy's newest (25 Nov 10:00), so the merge keeps the restore either way round: December pay 50,000, January the usual 300,000, no extra on the loan.

cases.title: AI1: a phone back after three weeks takes in a desktop copy two days fast: held at the phone's now plus 1 ms, `told` too, so a 09:00 check that day still counts the spend
cases.why: The phone was last used Sun 1 Nov 21:00 and is opened on Sun 22 Nov 12:00; a day ahead of its own now is Mon 23 Nov 12:00 [AH1]. The desktop's clock is two days fast: the 3,000 spend it took that morning (real 22 Nov 10:00) carries `told` and `at` Tue 24 Nov 10:00, 22 hours more than a day ahead, so it is held, at the phone's now plus 1 ms: 22 Nov 12:00:00.001 [AI1], marked `held: { came: 24 Nov 10:00, at: 22 Nov 12:00:00.001 }`, and the warning is shown [M4, N1]. Its `told` is held the same way, to 22 Nov 12:00:00.001 [AI1, N2]. The 48,000 check typed on the tablet at 22 Nov 09:00 is behind the phone's now and is kept as it came. So the spend reads as told at 12:00:00.001, after the 09:00 check: the check does not already hold it, and it counts as spending. Held at the newest `at` seen plus 1 ms (M4 before AI1) both `at` and `told` would read 1 Nov 21:00:00.001, three weeks before the check, and the spend would never be counted. e1 is the same on both copies and stays.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: AJ2: two pay-later plans added on two devices before they sync: both stay (confirm_review_5 h2)
cases.why: On Tue 24 Nov the phone, offline, adds a plan of 3 parts of 3,000 to the pay-later account (10:00); the desktop adds one of 6 parts of 5,000 (11:00). The record: 11:00 is newer, so the desktop's `at` and `by` win [D4]. `plans` is an array whose items all carry `id` and `at`, so it merges plan by plan by `id`, each by its own `at` [AJ2]: both plans stay, in id order. So on Sat 5 Dec 3,000 + 5,000 = 8,000 is due. Taken whole from the newer record, the phone's plan was lost and 5,000 was due, so safe to spend was 3,000 too high.

cases.question: merge_symmetric
cases.title: AJ2: the two plans merge the same way whichever copy is mine
cases.why: Each plan is settled by its own `at`, and a plan only one copy holds is kept, so the order of the copies changes nothing [AJ2, D4].

cases.question: merge
cases.title: AJ2: an empty `plans` on the newer copy keeps the other copy's plan
cases.why: The desktop, which has not seen the phone's 10:00 plan, renames the account at 11:00; its copy holds `plans: []`. The record: 11:00 wins, so the name is the desktop's [D4]. The shape is judged on either copy: the phone's items carry `id` and `at`, so `plans` is an entry list even though the desktop's is empty [AJ2, AJ-confirm]. A list the desktop never wrote to removes nothing, so the phone's plan stays (3 parts of 3,000 from 5 Dec).

cases.question: merge
cases.title: AJ2: a plan edited on one device and the account renamed on the other: both changes stay
cases.why: The phone corrects the plan to 4 parts at 12:00; the desktop, holding the plan as it was at 10:00, renames the account at 13:00. The record: 13:00 wins, so the name is the desktop's [D4]. The plan is settled by its own `at`: the phone's 12:00 beats the desktop's copy at 10:00, so it has 4 parts [AJ2]. Taken whole from the newer record, the plan went back to 3 parts and the fourth payment was never asked.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: AJ2: a plan removed on one device stays removed, though the other copy's record is newer
cases.why: The phone removes the plan at 12:00 (typed by mistake): it stays in the list with `gone` and its own `at` [M3]. The desktop renames the account at 13:00, still holding the plan at 10:00. The record: 13:00 wins [D4]; the plan: the removal at 12:00 beats the copy at 10:00, so it stays removed [AJ2, M3]. Taken whole from the newer record, it came back and its parts were asked again.

cases.question: restore
cases.title: AJ2: restoring an older backup stamps its plans and removes a plan added since
cases.why: On Wed 25 Nov 09:00 the phone restores a backup of Sun 22 Nov with the cloud on. The newest `at` it has seen is 24 Nov 13:00, so the restore's `at` is 25 Nov 09:00 [D4, AE5]. The account takes the backup's fields with that `at`; `told` stays 20 Nov [H1]. `plans` is found by its shape [AJ2] and restored as `steps` is: the backup's plan (3 parts) gets the new `at`, and the 6-part plan added on 24 Nov, not in the backup, is removed by its own `gone` (25 Nov) with the new `at` [M3, AB watch]. So the next merge keeps the restore; restored whole as a plain field, the cloud brought the 6-part plan back.

cases.question: merge

cases.why: The phone adds December's 5,000 to a list no build knows yet (`milestones`, 10:00); the desktop, which has not seen it, renames the goal at 11:00 with `milestones: []`. The name is the desktop's (11:00) [D4]. The shape is judged on either copy, so the empty list is an entry list and December stays [AI2, AJ2, AJ-confirm].

cases.question: merge
cases.title: AJ3: the home currency added on the phone and the country set on the desktop: both stay (confirm_review_5 h2)
cases.why: The person is moving home to the Philippines in April. On Tue 24 Nov the phone, offline, adds pesos from 1 Apr 2027 (10:00); the desktop, which has not seen it, sets the country to PH (11:00). `home` is a single record: 11:00 wins, so the country is PH [D4]. `home.curs` merges by `from`, each entry by its own `at` (SCHEMA_V3 2.1) [AJ3, AI2]: yen from 1 Nov and pesos from 1 Apr both stay, so the home currency changes in April. Taken whole from the newer `home`, only yen was left.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: AJ3: the minimum changed on the phone and the main bank on the desktop: `home` is one record, the newer wins whole
cases.why: `home` is a single record with one `at` (SCHEMA_V3 section 0): its plain fields come with the newer copy, as every record's do (mg-16) [D4]. The desktop's 11:00 wins, so the main bank is the new one and the minimum stays 20,000: the phone's 30,000 of 10:00 is lost, as a second device's edit of any other field of one record is. Only `curs`, an entry list, merges entry by entry [AJ3]. Whether `home`'s fields should merge one by one like the shared `ui` keys is listed as open question mg-q16.

cases.question: receive
cases.title: AJ3: a `home` that arrives more than a day ahead is held, its new currency entry too
cases.why: A tablet whose clock is two days fast writes `home` (country PH, pesos from April) at "Thu 26 Nov 10:00". The phone receives it at its own now, Tue 24 Nov 10:00: both `at`s are more than a day ahead, so each is held at that now plus 1 ms, 10:00:00.001, marked `held` with what it came with, and the warning is shown [M4, N1, AI1]. The yen entry (24 Nov 09:00) is not ahead and is left as it is. Then the merge: the held 10:00:00.001 beats the phone's 09:00, so PH and the peso entry are kept [AJ3, D4].

cases.why: The backup is of Sun 22 Nov: country JP, minimum 20,000, the old main bank, yen only. On Wed 25 Nov 09:00 the phone restores the backup with the cloud on: the restore's `at` is the later of 25 Nov 09:00 and 24 Nov 11:00:00.001, so 09:00 [D4, AE5]. `home` takes the backup's fields with that `at` and `by` [AB watch]; `curs` is an entry list, so the backup's yen entry gets the new `at` and the peso entry, not in the backup, is removed by its own `gone` (25 Nov) [AJ3, M3].

cases.question: devices
cases.title: AJ3: `home` used again after 23 and 45 days away (grid: home x used again after days away, AH1)
cases.why: Both devices were last used Sun 1 Nov 21:00. On Wed 11 Nov 10:00 the desktop adds pesos from April: the entry and `home` take its own clock, 11 Nov 10:00 [AH1]. The phone, unopened for 23 days, raises the minimum to 30,000 on Tue 24 Nov 12:00 without having seen that: `at` 24 Nov 12:00, its own clock, never held for the gap [AH1]. They sync within minutes, so nothing is held [M4]: `home` is the phone's (newer), and `curs` merges by `from`, so the desktop's peso entry stays [AJ3]. The phone, unopened for 45 days, is opened on Fri 8 Jan 2027: D8 asks the date first (mg-122), the person confirms, and the new main bank is written at 8 Jan 12:00, so the desktop ends with it, the 30,000 minimum and both currency entries.

cases.question: receive
cases.title: AJ4: a far-ahead edit held at the receiver's now plus 1 ms loses to an earlier edit from a slightly fast device
cases.why: The receiving phone's now is Tue 24 Nov 10:00. It has already taken in a copy from a device 30 minutes fast: the spend of 1,500 at "10:30", less than a day ahead, so not held [AH1]; the newest `at` it has seen is 10:30. Then a copy arrives from a tablet two days fast, with the same spend changed to 1,800 at "Thu 26 Nov 10:00": more than a day ahead, so it is held at the phone's own now plus 1 ms, 10:00:00.001, never at the newest seen plus 1 ms [AI1, AJ4], and the warning is shown. 10:00:00.001 is before 10:30, so the 1,500 stays, though the 1,800 may have been typed later. Which edit should win is unclear either way, and every device ends with the same copy (confirm_review_5); this case fixes the result [AJ4].

cases.question: devices
cases.title: AJ-confirm: two devices holding one far-ahead copy settle on the newer held `at` and the earliest `told` (the first to receive it)
cases.why: A tablet two days fast writes a spend at "Wed 25 Nov 10:00" (`told` the same). The phone receives it at its own now, Mon 23 Nov 09:00: held at 09:00:00.001, `told` too, marked `held: { came: 25 Nov 10:00, at: 09:00:00.001 }` [AI1, N2]. The desktop receives the same copy at 09:30: held at 09:30:00.001, `told` too, with its own mark. The phone's copy then reaches the desktop (09:40) and the desktop's reaches the phone (09:45): neither is ahead, and neither copy's `at` is the other's `came`, so nothing is held again. Two held copies of one record meet: the newer held `at` wins, 09:30:00.001 with the desktop's mark, and the earliest `told` is kept, 09:00:00.001 [AJ-confirm, H1]. The phone, which held it first, ends with that copy.

cases.question: devices
cases.title: AJ-confirm: the fast device itself ends with the same copy when the merged one comes back
cases.why: A tablet two days fast writes a spend at "Wed 25 Nov 10:00" (`told` the same). The phone receives it at its own now, Mon 23 Nov 09:00: held at 09:00:00.001, `told` too, marked `held: { came: 25 Nov 10:00, at: 09:00:00.001 }` [AI1, N2]. The desktop receives the same copy at 09:30: held at 09:30:00.001, `told` too, with its own mark. The phone's copy then reaches the desktop (09:40) and the desktop's reaches the phone (09:45): neither is ahead, and neither copy's `at` is the other's `came`, so nothing is held again. Two held copies of one record meet: the newer held `at` wins, 09:30:00.001 with the desktop's mark, and the earliest `told` is kept, 09:00:00.001 [AJ-confirm, H1]. The desktop's copy then reaches the tablet at its own (fast) now, 25 Nov 10:05: nothing in it is ahead. The tablet's own copy has `at` 25 Nov 10:00, the mark's `came`, so it is the same far-ahead write: it counts at the held 09:30:00.001 and takes the mark [N1]; `told` is the earliest, 09:00:00.001. All three devices show one copy.

open.question: `home` is one record with one `at`, so its plain fields (minBank, mainBank, country, mode) come with the newer copy whole: a minimum changed on the phone and a main bank changed on the desktop before they sync keep only the desktop's (mg-198). AJ3 merges `home.curs` by `from` but says nothing of the other fields. Should `home`'s fields merge one by one, each with its own `at`, like the shared `ui` keys (L merge q6, AF3)?
